update_log: Baseline initialization of India's operational Nuclear Power Plants and major High-Capacity Thermal Power Stations for Geography Static GK.

nuclear_power_plants.key_fact: India's first and oldest commercial nuclear power station; established in 1969 with the assistance of the United States.
The largest nuclear power station in India by installed capacity; built in collaboration with Russia (Rosatom).
Features India's first entirely indigenously developed 700 MW Pressurized Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR).
Set a world record in 2018 for the longest continuous operation of a nuclear reactor (962 days).
The only nuclear power plant in Uttar Pradesh, located on the banks of the river Ganga.
India's first fully indigenously constructed nuclear power station; also houses a Fast Breeder Test Reactor (FBTR).
India's second nuclear power plant; initially built with the collaboration of Canada (CANDU reactors).

major_thermal_power_plants.key_fact: The largest thermal power plant in India by installed capacity (over 4,760 MW), operated by NTPC.
One of the largest privately-owned coal power plants in the world, operated by Adani Power.
India's largest and most significant lignite-based power generation complex, operated by NLC India.
Operated by NTPC; notable for being one of the first plants in India to use supercritical boiler technology for higher efficiency.
A major NTPC plant in South India; its reservoir hosts India's largest floating solar PV project.
A massive NTPC pithead power station that sources coal directly from the nearby Mahanadi Coalfields.
The first multipurpose mega thermal power plant set up by the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC).
